texts.label: text
texts.orig: This procedure describes how to verify that the 5 V output pin of the Arduino Uno R3 supplies the correct regulated voltage, using a standard digital multimeter (DMM). The test is a non-destructive, in-circuit inspection and requires no firmware upload or code execution.
texts.text: This procedure describes how to verify that the 5 V output pin of the Arduino Uno R3 supplies the correct regulated voltage, using a standard digital multimeter (DMM). The test is a non-destructive, in-circuit inspection and requires no firmware upload or code execution.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: When  powered  via  USB,  the  Arduino  Uno  R3  receives  5  V  directly  from  the  host  bus.  When powered via the barrel jack, an onboard NCP1117ST50T3G linear voltage regulator steps the input voltage (7-12 V) down to a stable 5 V rail . This rail is exposed on the 5V pin (power header J1, pin 4) and serves as the primary supply for the ATmega328P microcontroller and all 5 V peripherals.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A voltage outside the specified tolerance indicates a fault in the USB supply, the onboard regulator, a solder defect, or an excessive load. This inspection must be performed before connecting any 5 V-sensitive peripheral.
texts.text: A voltage outside the specified tolerance indicates a fault in the USB supply, the onboard regulator, a solder defect, or an excessive load. This inspection must be performed before connecting any 5 V-sensitive peripheral.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: NOTE: No peripheral, shield, or load must be connected to the 5V pin during this measurement. An external load will cause a voltage drop and produce a misleading reading.
texts.text: NOTE: No peripheral, shield, or load must be connected to the 5V pin during this measurement. An external load will cause a voltage drop and produce a misleading reading.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Locate the power header (J1) on the Arduino Uno R3. It is the 8-pin single-row female header situated near the barrel jack connector. The 5V pin is the fourth pin from the end closest to the barrel jack, labelled "5V" in the silkscreen.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Ensure no shield, peripheral, or external wiring is attached to the Arduino. The board should be bare with only the USB cable connected.
texts.text: Ensure no shield, peripheral, or external wiring is attached to the Arduino. The board should be bare with only the USB cable connected.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Connect the Arduino to a USB host (PC, laptop, or powered USB hub) using the USB Type-A to Type-B cable. Confirm the green PWR LED illuminates steadily. Do not use the barrel jack for this test.
texts.text: Connect the Arduino to a USB host (PC, laptop, or powered USB hub) using the USB Type-A to Type-B cable. Confirm the green PWR LED illuminates steadily. Do not use the barrel jack for this test.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Set the DMM selector to DC Voltage (V-) mode. If the meter is not auto-ranging, select the range . Insert the red probe into the V/ W terminal and the black probe into the COM terminal.
texts.text: Set the DMM selector to DC Voltage (V-) mode. If the meter is not auto-ranging, select the range . Insert the red probe into the V/ W terminal and the black probe into the COM terminal.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Touch  the black  (COM)  probe firmly  to  any GND  pin on  the  board  (e.g.  J1-5  or  J1-6,  labelled GND). Maintain steady contact throughout the measurement.
texts.text: Touch  the black  (COM)  probe firmly  to  any GND  pin on  the  board  (e.g.  J1-5  or  J1-6,  labelled GND). Maintain steady contact throughout the measurement.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Touch the red probe firmly to the 5V pin (J1-4) . Ensure the probe tip makes clean contact with the metal pin and does not bridge to an adjacent pin.
texts.text: Touch the red probe firmly to the 5V pin (J1-4) . Ensure the probe tip makes clean contact with the metal pin and does not bridge to an adjacent pin.

texts.text: Step 6 - Read and record the voltage

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Allow the DMM reading to stabilise (typically <2 seconds). Read and record the displayed voltage to two decimal places.
texts.text: Allow the DMM reading to stabilise (typically <2 seconds). Read and record the displayed voltage to two decimal places.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Compare the recorded voltage against the acceptance criteria in Section 5. A reading of 4.75 V 5.25 V constitutes a PASS . Any reading outside this range constitutes a FAIL - refer to Section 7.
texts.text: Compare the recorded voltage against the acceptance criteria in Section 5. A reading of 4.75 V 5.25 V constitutes a PASS . Any reading outside this range constitutes a FAIL - refer to Section 7.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Remove both probes and disconnect the USB cable. Document the result in the test record (Section 8).
texts.text: Remove both probes and disconnect the USB cable. Document the result in the test record (Section 8).

texts.label: text
texts.orig: WARNING: Never connect the DMM probes across a live voltage source in resistance ( W ) or continuity mode. Always verify the DMM is set to DC Voltage before making contact with the board.
texts.text: WARNING: Never connect the DMM probes across a live voltage source in resistance ( W ) or continuity mode. Always verify the DMM is set to DC Voltage before making contact with the board.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: If the measured voltage falls outside 4.75 V - 5.25 V, perform the checks below in order before concluding that the board is defective.
